clue.text: One period on wreck by the sea

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it, so the later pieces come after the first

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil or wreck it
I is the Roman numeral for one
a period is a time

explanation.surface: Something from one era sits wrecked on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the one and the period follow the wreck, though 'on wreck' reads as a shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime means connected with the sea or living near the coast, a synonym of seaside.

clue.text: One interfering with sound tree

indicators.note: the word sound tells the solver that a meddler is heard, its spelling changing

parts.note: someone who interferes is a meddler

explanation.surface: Someone is meddling with a perfectly healthy tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective (healthy) describing the tree, but it signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: The medlar is a small fruit tree whose fruit is eaten when half-rotten.

clue.text: Getting up again, egret runs off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters going wrong or awry, so they are rearranged here

explanation.surface: A heron-like bird rises again and runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' asks for EGRET and RUNS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent describes something rising or reviving once more after a decline.

clue.text: Series of events in exercise

explanation.surface: A sequence of events happens during a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A train of events is a connected sequence; to train is to exercise or drill.

clue.text: Man has tea, squeezing lime over it

indicators.note: squeezing means one piece is pressed round another, holding it inside
over it suggests the word lime being turned over and rearranged

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea

explanation.surface: A man sits drinking tea and squeezes a lime over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over it' asks for the lime to be rearranged into MIEL, and 'squeezing' has that hold the tea, though the surface pictures lime juice squeezed over a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael is a common male first name, an example of a man's name.

clue.text: Part of bone shows mark made by weapon

parts.note: M abbreviates mark, the old German currency
an arrow is a weapon fired from a bow

explanation.surface: An X-ray of a bone shows the wound left by a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrow is the soft fatty tissue filling the cavities inside bones.

clue.text: Works not written in canon

parts.note: reads like music not composed as a round, but means writings left out of the accepted scriptures

explanation.surface: A composer's pieces were not written in the form of a canon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are biblical books excluded from the accepted scriptural canon.

clue.text: I must interrupt holiday for exam

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: A student's holiday is cut short by an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must interrupt' places I inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an examination taken again after failing it.

clue.text: Congratulations? The bloody opposite

explanation.surface: Someone offers congratulations, then swears it is quite the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as praise it means bravo; a steak cooked through is the opposite of a bloody, rare one.

clue.text: Spring into trench with speed

indicators.note: into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a ditch is a trench
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A soldier springs into a trench at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like a verb, but it is a noun, a SPA, put 'into' DITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch means promptness or haste, a synonym of quickness.

clue.text: Shortly to advise foreign representative

indicators.note: shortly here means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to consult is to seek or give advice

explanation.surface: A diplomat will advise shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' cuts the last letter T from CONSULT.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is an official appointed by a state to look after its citizens abroad.

clue.text: Show contempt for suggestions that are raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: tips are hints or suggestions

explanation.surface: Someone scorns ideas that are put forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are raised' reads TIPS upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit at someone, or spit on something, is to show utter scorn.

clue.text: Masonic garment for the stage

explanation.surface: A Freemason's regalia is worn for a theatre performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons wear ceremonial aprons; the apron is the part of a stage projecting in front of the curtain.

clue.text: Made breathy sound, when robber died

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a pirate is a robber at sea

explanation.surface: Someone gasped when the robber died.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirated sound is pronounced with an audible puff of breath.

clue.text: Clever ballad reaching the heart is oral

indicators.note: reaching the heart of the words means the run sits inside them, across the word gap

explanation.surface: A clever ballad that touches the heart is performed by mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'Clever ballad', across the gap between the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbal can mean spoken rather than written, as in a verbal agreement.

clue.text: British don't have somewhere to swim? Try here

definitions.text: British don't have somewhere to swim? Try here

parts.note: to lack something is not to have it
a pool is a place to swim

explanation.surface: Britons short of a swimming pool are told to go to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: BLACKPOOL is a big seaside resort in north-west England; the whole clue suggests swimming in the sea there.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside resort is where Britons without a pool might bathe, in the sea.

clue.text: Swerve on ball — place backwards to leg

indicators.note: backwards tells us to read the word for place from right to left

parts.note: a spot is a place
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A bowler's ball swerves, landing so as to turn to the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns SPOT into TOPS. 'leg' is cricket's leg side in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Topspin is forward rotation given to a ball, making it dip or kick.

clue.text: One ruling no wine must be used in meat dish

indicators.note: used in suggests one ingredient going inside another, so the pieces are placed within

parts.note: pate is a paste of meat or liver
O is zero or nothing
tent is a dark red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A ruler insists on no wine being used in cooking a meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be used in' signals the container. TENT, a sweet dark red wine from Spain, is an old crossword favourite; 'no' gives O, not a negative.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or ruler with great power.

clue.text: Wicked, grabbing money drawer, and going to prison

indicators.note: grabbing means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: base means low or wicked
a till is a cash drawer

explanation.surface: A wicked thief steals from the till and is sent to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' signals the container. The Bastille was the Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789, so the name stands for any prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the famous Paris jail, and the name is used for any prison.

clue.text: Interest in a wide area of speech

indicators.note: of speech tells us the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a tract is a wide area of land

explanation.surface: Someone takes an interest in a broad field of linguistics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of speech' says 'a tract', spoken, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To interest someone is to draw or appeal to them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Journey to game, getting a lift

indicators.note: in a down clue a lift raises the letters, so they read upward

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: Someone travels to a match by hitching a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting a lift' turns RU upward in this down clue, giving UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a trip or journey taking in several places.

clue.text: Embarrassed about soldier's song

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: shy means bashful or embarrassed
a soldier ant is an ant, so the soldier gives ANT

explanation.surface: Someone sings a soldier's song, embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. 'soldier' misleads toward a military song; it is the soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a sailors' work song.

clue.text: Angry about article's expression of dismissive finality

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: sore can mean angry or resentful
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone angry about a newspaper article ends the argument dismissively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'article' is the grammatical one, not a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a childish retort ending an argument, like 'that settles it'.

clue.text: Brick may be aimed at goal

explanation.surface: A brick is hurled at the goalmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: In bricklaying a header is a brick laid end-on; in football it is a shot with the head.

clue.text: Make way to clubs, say one assumed for exercise

parts.note: to track is to follow a path or make one's way
clubs is an example of a suit of cards

explanation.surface: Someone makes their way to the golf clubs, dressed for a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs, say' points to golf clubs in the surface, but means the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing you put on is assumed, and this garment is worn for sport and training.

clue.text: Representative tucked into beer and stout

indicators.note: tucked into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: ale is a beer
an MP is a member of parliament, a representative

explanation.surface: A politician tucks into beer and stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' signals the container. 'stout' looks like a second beer but is the definition, meaning plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample can describe a large, generous figure, as stout does.

clue.text: Crooner taking drug overdose

parts.note: Bing Crosby was a famous crooner
E is ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A singer takes too much of a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of excessive indulgence, a synonym of a spree of overdoing it.

clue.text: One's mounted stand for funeral to see king buried

indicators.note: buried means the letter is put inside the word

parts.note: a bier is a stand on which a coffin is placed
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king is laid on a funeral stand before burial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried' puts K inside BIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcyclist rides astride a machine, so they are someone mounted.

clue.text: On stage, the best little machine

parts.note: a lap is one stage of a race or journey
top means the best

explanation.surface: An actor on stage is the best.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a small portable computer.

clue.text: Sailor getting his cards, in two ways

parts.note: a deck is a pack of cards
a hand is the cards held by a player

explanation.surface: A sailor is sacked in two different ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in two ways' means 'cards' is read twice, as DECK and as HAND. 'Getting his cards' is British for being fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a crew member doing manual work on a ship's deck.

clue.text: Archdeacon seen in diocese regularly

indicators.note: seen in means one piece is visible inside another

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city and diocese
Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: An archdeacon is seen around the diocese at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' signals the container. 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letters signal but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means uniformly or at steady intervals.

clue.text: Pay attention repeatedly for sound of encouragement

indicators.note: repeatedly asks for the word to appear twice in a row

parts.note: to hear is to listen or pay attention

explanation.surface: Listen again and again for cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles HEAR. The phrase is the cry of approval in the British parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry is shouted to show agreement and support for a speaker.
